# Prompt caching — concept pack

> Prompt caching lets the API reuse an already-processed prompt prefix (tools → system → messages) across requests to cut cost and latency: Anthropic offers automatic caching or explicit `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` breakpoints with 5-minute or 1-hour TTLs, bills cache writes at 1.25×/2× and cache hits at 0.1× the base input price, and reports them in usage.cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens; OpenRouter passes cache_control through to Anthropic and Gemini, adds provider sticky routing, and documents OpenAI automatic caching. Two of the three docsets contributed (the OpenAI export is empty).

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.3.0 · generated 2026-08-31 · 176 units · 2 sources · rights: extractive -->

## Definitions

- [definition] Automatic caching — Automatic caching is the simplest way to enable prompt caching. Instead of placing `cache_control` on individual content blocks, add a single `cache_control` field at the top level of your request body. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#automatic-caching · keywords: automatic caching, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Prompt caching — Prompt caching doesn't reduce the number of tokens in context, but it reduces what you pay for them on subsequent requests. If your tool definitions are stable, cache them once and reuse the cached prefix across thousands of requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context#prompt-caching · keywords: cache prefix, prompt caching
- [definition] Cache miss reason types — `cache_miss_reason` is a discriminated union on `type`. The response reports the earliest divergence only, so fix it first; later ones may be hidden behind it. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#cache-miss-reason-types · keywords: cache diagnostics, cache hit
- [definition] Caching — Some endpoints/models provide implicit caching of prompts. This keeps repeated prompt data in an in-memory cache in the provider's datacenter, so that the repeated part of the prompt does not need to be re-processed. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/zdr#caching · keywords: automatic caching · note: OpenRouter's description of provider implicit caching

## Structure and components

- [definition] Cache storage and sharing — Prompt caching uses [workspace](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)-level isolation. Caches are isolated per workspace, ensuring data separation between workspaces within the same organization. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#cache-storage-and-sharing · keywords: cache storage and sharing, prompt caching
- [definition] Advisor prompt caching — There are two independent caching layers. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-prompt-caching · keywords: prompt caching

## How it works

- [definition] How it works — Set `max_tokens: 0` in your request. The API reads your prompt into the model and writes the cache at any `cache_control` breakpoint, then returns immediately without generating any output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#how-it-works · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache pre-warming, cache write, cache_control
- [definition] How automatic caching works in multi-turn conversations — With automatic caching, the cache point moves forward automatically as conversations grow. Each new request caches everything up to the last cacheable block, and previous content is read from cache. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#how-automatic-caching-works-in-multi-turn-conversations · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, cacheable, prompt caching
- [definition] Explicit cache breakpoints — For more control over caching, you can place `cache_control` directly on individual content blocks. This is useful when you need to cache different sections that change at different frequencies, or need fine-grained control over exactly what gets cached. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#explicit-cache-breakpoints · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache_control, explicit caching, prompt caching
- [definition] Server tool results are cached automatically — When your request has prompt caching enabled and Claude uses a [server tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) such as web search, web fetch, or code execution, the API automatically places a cache breakpoint on the server tool result before running the… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#server-tool-results-are-cached-automatically · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Implicit Caching — Gemini 2.5 series models and newer support **implicit caching**, providing automatic caching functionality similar to OpenAI’s automatic caching. Implicit caching works seamlessly — no manual setup or additional `cache_control` breakpoints required. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#implicit-caching · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Provider Sticky Routing — To maximize cache hit rates, OpenRouter uses **provider sticky routing** to route your subsequent requests to the same provider endpoint after a cached request. This works automatically with both implicit caching (e.g. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#provider-sticky-routing · keywords: automatic caching, cache hit, prompt caching, sticky routing
- [definition] Combining with block-level caching — Automatic caching is compatible with [explicit cache breakpoints](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#explicit-cache-breakpoints). When used together, the automatic cache breakpoint uses one of the 4 available breakpoint slots. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#combining-with-block-level-caching · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, explicit caching, prompt caching
- [definition] When to use a mid-conversation system message — [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) hashes the request prefix in order: `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`. A cache hit requires the prefix to match a recent request exactly, byte for byte, up to the cache breakpoint. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages#when-to-use-a-mid-conversation-system-message · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache hit, cache prefix, prompt caching
- [definition] Caching in the Batch API — `cache_control` breakpoints work on Anthropic `:batch` endpoints the same way as on the sync API, but the requests inside a single batch may process concurrently and in any order — a cache written by one line is not guaranteed to be visible to other lines in the same batch. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#caching-in-the-batch-api · keywords: Message Batches, cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Prompt caching — Compaction works well with [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching). You can add a `cache_control` breakpoint on compaction blocks to cache the summarized content. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction#prompt-caching · keywords: Message Batches, cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Pre-warming the cache — Cache pre-warming lets you load your system prompt or tool definitions into the prompt cache before a user triggers a real request. This eliminates the cache-miss latency penalty on the first user interaction, reducing time-to-first-token (TTFT) for latency-sensitive applications. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#pre-warming-the-cache · keywords: cache hit, cache pre-warming, prompt caching
- [definition] Executor-side caching — The `advisor_tool_result` block is cacheable like any other content block. A `cache_control` breakpoint placed after it on a subsequent turn hits. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#executor-side-caching · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache_control, cacheable
- [definition] What invalidates your cache — The cache follows a prefix hierarchy (`tools` → `system` → `messages`), so a change at one level invalidates that level and everything after it: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#what-invalidates-your-cache · keywords: cache invalidation, cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [definition] Prompt Caching — Discovering a tool does not disturb the tools already in the conversation, so prompt caching is preserved across a search. You can start a conversation with a small loaded set, let the model discover more as it goes, and keep your cache hit across every turn. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools/tool-search#prompt-caching · keywords: Message Batches, cache hit, prompt caching
- [definition] Using prompt caching with Message Batches — The Message Batches API supports prompt caching, allowing you to potentially reduce costs and processing time for batch requests. The pricing discounts from prompt caching and Message Batches can stack, providing even greater cost savings when both features are used together. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#using-prompt-caching-with-message-batches · keywords: Message Batches, cache pricing, prompt caching
- [definition] Prompt caching in manual mode — Manual mode adds one rule on top of the mode-neutral caching behavior described in [thinking and prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#thinking-and-prompt-caching): changing `budget_tokens` between requests invalidates cache breakpoints, just as switching… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking#prompt-caching-in-manual-mode · keywords: cache breakpoint, prompt caching
- [parameter] [Tool search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool): Discovered tools load as `tool_reference` blocks, preserving prefix cache — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: Message Batches, cache_control
- [definition] defer\_loading and cache preservation — Deferred tools are not included in the system-prompt prefix. When the model discovers a deferred tool through [tool search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool), the definition is appended inline as a `tool_reference` block in the conversation history. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#defer-loading-and-cache-preservation · keywords: Message Batches, cache_control
- [definition] Cache-aware ITPM — Many API providers use a combined "tokens per minute" (TPM) limit that may include all tokens, both cached and uncached, input and output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits#cache-aware-itpm · keywords: cache pricing, cache-aware rate limits
- [definition] Prompt caching — Consecutive requests that keep the same thinking configuration and effort level preserve prompt caching; see [Thinking and prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#thinking-and-prompt-caching) for the full rules. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-steering-and-cost#prompt-caching · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] `defer_loading` and prompt caching — Tools with `defer_loading: true` are stripped from the rendered tools section before the cache key is computed. They don't appear in the system-prompt prefix at all. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-reference#defer-loading-and-prompt-caching · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Mid-conversation tool changes (beta) — You can add or remove tools between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache, instead of resending a fixed tool list for the life of a session. Mid-conversation tool changes are in beta: include the `mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01` beta header in your requests. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5/whats-new-opus-5#mid-conversation-tool-changes-beta · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Session Stickiness — The Pareto Router reuses the selected **model** and **provider** on a best-effort basis so that subsequent requests in the same conversation route to the same place. This keeps behavior consistent within a conversation and maximizes [prompt cache](/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching) hits. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/pareto-router#session-stickiness · keywords: prompt caching · note: OpenRouter Pareto Router
- [definition] How cache diagnostics works — When the beta header is present, the API stores a lightweight fingerprint of each request, keyed by the response `id`. On your next request, include that `id` as `diagnostics.previous_message_id`. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#how-cache-diagnostics-works · keywords: cache diagnostics

## How-to and procedures

- [definition] Mixing different TTLs — You can use both 1-hour and 5-minute cache controls in the same request, but with an important constraint: Cache entries with longer TTL must appear before shorter TTLs (that is, a 1-hour cache entry must appear before any 5-minute cache entries). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#mixing-different-ttls · keywords: cache TTL, cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] cache\_control on tool definitions — Place `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` on the last tool in your `tools` array. This caches the entire tool-definitions prefix, from the first tool through the marked breakpoint: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#cache-control-on-tool-definitions · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache prefix, cache_control, ephemeral cache_control type
- [idea] Consider using the 1-hour cache duration with prompt caching for batches with shared context to improve cache hit rates, as processing can take longer than 5 minutes. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works · keywords: Message Batches, cache TTL, cache hit, prompt caching
- [definition] Structuring your prompt — Place static content (tool definitions, system instructions, context, examples) at the beginning of your prompt. Mark the end of the reusable content for caching using the `cache_control` parameter. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#structuring-your-prompt · keywords: cache prefix, cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] How to Enable Gemini Prompt Caching: — Gemini caching in OpenRouter requires you to insert `cache_control` breakpoints explicitly within message content, similar to Anthropic. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#how-to-enable-gemini-prompt-caching · keywords: cache breakpoint, cache_control, prompt caching
- [idea] Use prompt caching to reduce cost and latency by caching prompt prefixes shared across requests in a batch. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#next-steps · keywords: Message Batches, cache prefix, prompt caching
- [definition] When to use the 1-hour cache — If you have prompts that are used at a regular cadence (that is, system prompts that are used more frequently than every 5 minutes), continue to use the 5-minute cache, because this will continue to be refreshed at no additional charge. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#when-to-use-the-1-hour-cache · keywords: cache TTL, prompt caching
- [definition] Using `session_id` for sticky sessions — For more explicit control over sticky routing, you can pass a `session_id` in your request. When a `session_id` is present, OpenRouter uses it directly as the sticky routing key instead of deriving one from message hashing. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#using-session-id-for-sticky-sessions · keywords: prompt caching, sticky routing
- [definition] Modifying tool results — You can modify tool results before they're sent back to Claude. This is useful for adding metadata such as `cache_control` to enable [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) on tool results, or for transforming the tool output. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-runner#modifying-tool-results · keywords: cache_control, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Shrink Tool-Heavy Prefixes**: Recommended Configuration=`openrouter:tool_search` + `defer_loading: true`; Latency Impact=Defer most tool definitions out of the prompt; keeps cacheable prefix lean and stable across turns. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/latency-and-performance#quick-reference-summary · keywords: cache prefix, cacheable
- [definition] Reading diagnostics alongside usage — `diagnostics` answers "did my request change?" while `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` answers "did the cache hit?". Combining them tells you where to look. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#reading-diagnostics-alongside-usage · keywords: cache hit, cache_read_input_tokens
- [definition] Combining approaches — These approaches compose. A long-running agent might use tool search to keep the toolset lean, prompt caching to amortize the cost of the remaining definitions, and context editing to trim stale results as the conversation grows. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context#combining-approaches · keywords: Message Batches, prompt caching
- [definition] Cut spend without losing quality — Prompt caching, token hygiene, batch processing, and a prompt audit against your current model all lower what you pay without lowering output quality. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#cut-spend-without-losing-quality · keywords: Message Batches, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Agent Loops / Long Contexts**: Recommended Configuration=Stable `session_id` + static prompt prefix; Latency Impact=Slashes prefill time and cost (up to 80–90%) via provider KV cache. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/latency-and-performance#quick-reference-summary · keywords: KV cache, cache prefix
- [fact] System messages must be placed after the user turn to keep cached bytes untouched and satisfy placement rules. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example
- [definition] Advisor-side caching — Set `caching` on the tool definition to enable prompt caching for the advisor's own transcript across calls within the same conversation: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool#advisor-side-caching · keywords: prompt caching
- [parameter] Any workload, any model: Do this=Turn on prompt caching and trim unneeded tokens; both are free; Where=[Cache repeated context](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#cache-repeated-context) · [Trim tokens](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#trim-input-and-context-tokens) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#start-here · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Basic usage — Send the beta header on every turn. On the first turn, pass `"previous_message_id": null` to opt in without a prior message to compare against. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#basic-usage · keywords: cache diagnostics
- [definition] Threading diagnostics through a conversation loop — In a multi-turn conversation, carry the latest response `id` forward as `previous_message_id` on every turn. The first iteration passes `null` to opt in; each subsequent iteration passes the `id` from the previous response. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#threading-diagnostics-through-a-conversation-loop · keywords: cache diagnostics
- [definition] Cache control — Add `cache_control` on the search result block to cache it for reuse across requests. It sits alongside `citations` on the same block: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/search-results#cache-control · keywords: cache_control
- [parameter] A person waits between turns: Do this=Use the 1-hour cache duration; it is cheaper once about 1 turn in 20 follows a pause between 5 minutes and an hour and few gaps run over an hour; Where=[Pick the cache duration](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#pick-the-cache-duration) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence#start-here · keywords: cache TTL
- [definition] User tracking — Track your end-users by including a `user` parameter in API requests. This improves caching performance (sticky routing per user) and enables user-level analytics in your activity feed and exports. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/get-started/enterprise-quickstart#user-tracking · keywords: sticky routing

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [problem] Automatic prompt caching using the top-level `cache_control` field is not supported; explicit cache breakpoints must be used instead. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-on-amazon-bedrock-legacy#feature-support · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, cache_control, explicit caching · note: scope: Claude on Amazon Bedrock (legacy) page only — on the Claude API the top-level cache_control IS supported (see Automatic caching)
- [definition] Prompt caching considerations — If you use [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), changing the Skills list in your container breaks the cache. Skills render into the system prompt in a fixed order, so the same list produces the same cacheable prefix: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/skills-guide#prompt-caching-considerations · keywords: cache invalidation, cache prefix, cacheable, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Tool definitions**: Tools cache=✘; System cache=✘; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: cache invalidation, prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Tool choice**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✓; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Changes to `tool_choice` parameter only affect message blocks — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: cache invalidation, prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Images**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✓; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Adding/removing images anywhere in the prompt affects message blocks — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: cache invalidation, prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [concept] Prompt caching is supported in the Message Batches API, but cache hits are provided on a best-effort basis due to concurrent and unordered processing. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#faq · keywords: Message Batches, cache hit, cache pricing, prompt caching
- [parameter] [Web search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool): Enabling or disabling invalidates the system and messages caches — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache invalidation, cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [parameter] [Web fetch](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool): Enabling or disabling invalidates the system and messages caches — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache invalidation, cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [definition] Mid-conversation tool changes — The `tools` array sits even earlier in the hashed request prefix than the top-level `system` field, so editing it invalidates the [prompt cache](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) for the entire conversation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages#mid-conversation-tool-changes · keywords: cache invalidation, cache prefix, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Non-tool results passed to extended thinking requests**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✓; Messages cache=Model-specific; Impact=On Opus 4.5+ and Sonnet 4.6+, thinking blocks are preserved by default, so the cache remains valid (✓). On earlier Opus/Sonnet models and all Haiku models, all previously-cached thinking blocks are stripped from context, and any messages that follow those thinking… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: Message Batches, prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [problem] Setting `max_tokens` to 0 is not supported inside a batch because ephemeral cache entries written during processing likely expire before follow-up requests run. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing#how-the-message-batches-api-works · keywords: Message Batches, cache breakpoint, ephemeral cache_control type
- [parameter] **Web search toggle**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✘; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Enabling/disabling web search modifies the system prompt — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Citations toggle**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✘; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Enabling/disabling citations modifies the system prompt — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Speed setting**: Tools cache=✓; System cache=✘; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Switching between [`speed: "fast"` and standard speed](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode) invalidates system and message caches — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Thinking parameters**: Tools cache=Model-specific; System cache=Model-specific; Messages cache=✘; Impact=The thinking configuration (mode, and `budget_tokens` in extended mode) is rendered into the prompt, so changing it always invalidates message blocks; tool and system caches are also invalidated on models that render the configuration ahead of them. See [Thinking and prompt… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [parameter] **Effort setting**: Tools cache=Model-specific; System cache=Model-specific; Messages cache=✘; Impact=Changing the [`output_config.effort`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) value always invalidates message blocks, with the same model-specific effect on tool and system caches as thinking parameters. Setting effort explicitly to the model's default is equivalent to… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: prefix hierarchy, prompt caching
- [definition] Limitations — A `max_tokens: 0` request is rejected with an `invalid_request_error` if any of the following are set, since each implies output that a zero-token budget cannot produce: — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#limitations · keywords: cache pre-warming, prompt caching
- [definition] What invalidates the cache — Modifications to cached content can invalidate some or all of the cache. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache · keywords: cache invalidation, prompt caching
- [definition] Cache hits drop after changing thinking settings — `cache_read_input_tokens` falls to zero on requests that previously hit the cache. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting#cache-hits-drop-after-changing-thinking-settings · keywords: cache hit, cache pricing, cache_read_input_tokens
- [parameter] Modifying tool definitions: Entire cache (tools, system, messages) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#what-invalidates-your-cache · keywords: cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [parameter] Toggling web search or citations: System and messages caches — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#what-invalidates-your-cache · keywords: cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [parameter] Changing `tool_choice`: Messages cache — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#what-invalidates-your-cache · keywords: cache_control, prefix hierarchy
- [parameter] Changing `disable_parallel_tool_use`: Messages cache — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#what-invalidates-your-cache · keywords: cache_control, prefix hierarchy

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [definition] What stays the same — Automatic caching uses the same underlying caching infrastructure. Pricing, minimum token thresholds, context ordering requirements, and the 20-block lookback window all apply the same as with explicit breakpoints. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-stays-the-same · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, minimum cacheable prompt length, prefix hierarchy
- [definition] Explicit Prompt Caching — Automatic prompt caching still works with no code changes. Explicit caching adds direct control over cache boundaries instead of relying on OpenAI's automatic breakpoint placement. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/model-migrations/gpt-5-6#explicit-prompt-caching · keywords: automatic caching, cache breakpoint, explicit caching, prompt caching
- [parameter] Prompt caching: What it reduces=Token cost of repeated tool definitions; When it fits=Stable toolsets across many requests; Learn more=[Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context#the-four-approaches · keywords: prompt caching

## Changes and history

- [definition] Replacing the max\_tokens=1 workaround — Before `max_tokens: 0` was available, some applications used `max_tokens: 1` warm-up calls to achieve the same effect. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#replacing-the-max-tokens1-workaround · keywords: cache pre-warming, prompt caching
- [definition] GPT-5.6 Migration Guide — Adopt reasoning.mode, reasoning.context, and explicit prompt caching for the GPT-5.6 model family — https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/model-migrations/gpt-5-6#gpt-56-migration-guide · keywords: explicit caching, prompt caching
- [snippet] Python: client.beta.prompt_caching.messages.create(**params) — `client.beta.prompt_caching.messages.create(**params)` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#faq · keywords: prompt caching · note: deprecated beta namespace, quoted from a TypeError FAQ; current SDKs use client.messages.create with cache_control on blocks
- [snippet] TypeScript: client.beta.promptCaching.messages.create(/* ... */); — `client.beta.promptCaching.messages.create(/* ... */);` — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#faq · keywords: prompt caching · note: deprecated beta namespace, quoted from a TypeError FAQ; current SDKs use client.messages.create with cache_control on blocks

## Facts and statements

- [parameter] [Code execution](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool): Container state is independent of prompt cache — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache_control, prompt caching
- [definition] Grouping requests across modalities — Beyond sticky routing, OpenRouter uses `session_id` to group your requests in the [Sessions view on the Logs page](https://openrouter.ai/logs?tab=sessions). One `session_id` links requests across conversation turns, retries, and different modalities. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#grouping-requests-across-modalities · keywords: prompt caching, sticky routing
- [parameter] [Fallback credit](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fallback-credit): Description=Avoid paying the prompt-cache cost twice when you retry a refused request on another model. The refusal carries a credit token, and echoing it on the retry bills the retry as though the conversation had been on the new model all along. Message Batches results do not include fallback credit… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview#model-capabilities · keywords: Message Batches, prompt caching · note: fallback credit: retrying a refused request without paying the cache twice
- [definition] Supported Models and Limitations: — Only certain Gemini models support caching. Please consult Google's [Gemini API Pricing Documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) for the most current details. — https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching#supported-models-and-limitations · keywords: prompt caching
- [parameter] [Text editor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/text-editor-tool): Standard client tool, no special caching interaction — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache_control
- [parameter] [Bash](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool): Standard client tool, no special caching interaction — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache_control
- [parameter] [Memory](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool): Standard client tool, no special caching interaction — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#per-tool-interaction-table · keywords: cache_control
- [definition] Feature compatibility — Citations work in conjunction with other API features including [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting), and [batch… — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations#feature-compatibility · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Supported models — Prompt caching (both automatic and explicit) is supported on all [active Claude models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#supported-models · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Data retention — Prompt caching (both automatic and explicit) is ZDR eligible. Anthropic does not store the raw text of your prompts or Claude's responses. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#data-retention · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Mechanics — Three mechanics follow from Claude managing its own thinking: turn validation, prompt caching, and how you bound cost. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-steering-and-cost#mechanics · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Prompt caching — For how `defer_loading` preserves prompt caching, see [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool#prompt-caching · keywords: prompt caching
- [definition] Prompt caching — For caching tool definitions across turns, see [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching). — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#prompt-caching · keywords: prompt caching · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool
- [definition] Billing — You are not billed for a request that is refused before any output is generated. When you retry on another model, [fallback credit](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fallback-credit) refunds the prompt-cache cost of switching, so you avoid paying that cost twice. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5/introducing-claude-fable-5-and-claude-mythos-5#billing · keywords: prompt caching · note: fallback credit: retrying a refused request without paying the cache twice
- [definition] Mid-Conversation Tool Changes (Beta) — Opus 5 supports [changing the available tool set between turns](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages#mid-conversation-tool-changes) without invalidating the prompt cache, using system-role content blocks: — https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/model-migrations/opus-5#mid-conversation-tool-changes-beta · keywords: prompt caching
- [fact] The top-level `system` field never changes in this example to ensure the cached prefix stays intact. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-effort-example · keywords: cache prefix
- [definition] Data retention — Cache diagnostics is ZDR eligible (qualified). Anthropic does not store the raw text of your prompts or Claude's outputs for this feature. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/cache-diagnostics#data-retention · keywords: cache diagnostics
- [parameter] Must match exactly: `system`, `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `thinking`, and `cache_control`, plus `output_config`, `mcp_servers`, `context_management`, and `container` when you use them — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fallback-credit#reference · keywords: cache_control · note: fallback credit: retrying a refused request without paying the cache twice
- [definition] Checking that the credit applied — The refund is visible in the retry's `usage`. Compared with what the same request would report without the token, `cache_creation_input_tokens` is lower, and `cache_read_input_tokens` is higher by the same amount. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fallback-credit#checking-that-the-credit-applied · keywords: cache_read_input_tokens · note: fallback credit: retrying a refused request without paying the cache twice
- [parameter] `usage.prompt_tokens_details`: Always empty — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/openai-sdk#response-fields · keywords: cache_read_input_tokens · note: scope: the OpenAI SDK compatibility layer of the Claude API — the field is always empty there; OpenRouter does populate prompt_tokens_details

## Related concepts

- cacheable — variant · 7 units · the docs' adjective for content the prompt cache can hold
- cache_control — part · 45 units · Anthropic/OpenRouter per-block cache marker
- cache breakpoint — part · 27 units
- prefix hierarchy — part · 21 units · tools → system → messages; a change at one level invalidates it and everything after
- cache diagnostics — part · 16 units · Anthropic beta that reports why a cache missed
- cache prefix — part · 10 units · the cache key is the exact request prefix: tools → system → messages
- cache storage and sharing — part · 2 units · who can hit whose cache
- automatic caching — hyponym · 13 units · provider places the cache point (Anthropic auto mode, OpenAI, Gemini implicit)
- explicit caching — hyponym · 5 units · caller places cache_control breakpoints
- ephemeral cache_control type — instance · 4 units · the only cache_control type; bare 'ephemeral' excluded (containers)
- cache hit — measure · 26 units
- cache pricing — measure · 24 units · pricing multipliers and table columns; MTok alone is any price table
- cache write — measure · 20 units
- cache TTL — measure · 12 units
- cache_read_input_tokens — measure · 10 units · usage/pricing fields reported per response
- cache read — measure · 6 units
- minimum cacheable prompt length — measure · 3 units · per-model token floors below which nothing is cached
- cache invalidation — problem · 11 units · what changes cause the prefix to stop matching
- KV cache — near-synonym · 2 units · model-internal attention state; prompt caching is the API feature built on it
- response caching — contrast · no units in scope · OpenRouter feature that replays a whole response for an identical request — not prompt caching
- cache pre-warming — dependent · 5 units · loading the cache before real traffic
- sticky routing — dependent · 5 units · OpenRouter: routing follow-up requests to the provider holding the cache
- cache-aware rate limits — dependent · 2 units · Anthropic: cache reads excluded from input-tokens-per-minute
- Message Batches — related · 18 units · features whose interaction with the prompt cache the docs describe; never qualifies a unit alone
